payload.selection_rationale: The single practice proposal is taken as the core because it fits how the store is already built, and its choices survive the measurements. The store is a flat column store with fixed 64Ki pages and a contiguous child block per folder (FirstChild/ChildCount), and each entry already has Parent, Charges() and a first-seen FileId index. Adding three rollup columns and posting each charged file up the Parent chain at append time extends that shape and needs no new structure. It also keeps totals exact at any cut, including a cancelled scan, and needs no completion signal from the Scanner (a 'settle with no reader' hazard this engine has met before). It fits the spikes. The ID set stays key-only (the index holds entry indices and reads the ID columns), so the Dictionary that went over 1 GiB is never needed. Nothing in the design needs the first holder's index. The single-writer, deterministic-order invariant is written down because first-seen charging with 16 workers was a no-go. It rests on the survey's finding that the Scanner is a single-threaded DFS, and it makes criterion 2's test valid. I changed six things: (1) The brute-force oracle recomputes expected totals from the test's own input model. The proposal's oracle summed the store's ChargedSize, so a Charges() defect could hide behind it. (2) I dropped the share clamp, the JIT-optimised guard and the claim of exactness for concurrent readers. None of them can be tested or needed by this slice. (3) TryAddFileId becomes private, so the compiler stops the Scanner calling it and charging a file nowhere. (4) Append rejects a parent index not yet in the store, so the ancestor walk cannot loop. (5) TopLevelTracker is pinned to the rollups with an equality assertion, because the proposal missed that it is a second accumulator of the same numbers. (6) I downgraded two prior-art entries from cited to recalled because their URLs are not in the fetched block I was handed.

components.name: Rollup columns
components.responsibility: Adds RolledSize (long), RolledOnDisk (long) and FilesBelow (int) to each row of the existing 64Ki-entry Page, about 20 B/row, meaningful on folder rows only. File and Link rows answer from Charges(), so a file's charge has exactly one source. Pages stay fixed and are never reallocated.
components.key_interactions: Gated by the existing ScanStoreBudgetTests.FiveMillionEntriesFitTheMemoryBudget, which must pass unchanged with the columns present. If it does not, the pre-decided fallback is a 4 B per-row folder-slot column plus 20 B per folder, behind the same accessors, so no contract moves.

components.name: Charge rule
components.responsibility: Charges() returns (Size, OnDisk) only for an EntryKind.File that is not HardlinkDuplicate. Folder (readable or Unreadable) and Link return (0, 0) whatever sizes they state. This closes the survey gap where an Unreadable folder with a stated size still charged it.
components.key_interactions: Read by the append posting, by the rollup reads for file rows, by the Scanner's totals and TopLevelTracker feed, and by SL-040's LargestFiles (files only, so unaffected).

components.name: Append posting and first-seen dedup
components.responsibility: The store's existing entry-append does four things in order. (1) It validates the parent: the index must already exist, and the parent must be a Folder not flagged Unreadable, otherwise it throws. (2) It writes the row and clears any caller-supplied HardlinkDuplicate bit, because the store is the only source of that flag. (3) For a File with a non-zero 128-bit ID it registers the ID through TryAddFileId, now private to the store, and sets HardlinkDuplicate if the ID was already present. (4) For a File it walks parent, then Parent(parent), up to the root in a while loop (never recursion), adding Charges() to RolledSize/RolledOnDisk and 1 to FilesBelow. Folder and Link appends post nothing.
components.key_interactions: This is the only place a charge enters the totals. If the Scanner changes a file's Size or OnDisk after the append (SizeProbe), that goes through one new store method that posts the old-to-new charge delta up the same chain. If every probe happens before the append, the method is not added. The builder settles which with one grep of Scanner.cs. The XML doc states the two caller obligations: one writer thread, and deterministic append order (parent before children, each folder's children as one contiguous block in listing order).

components.name: Rollup reads and ordered children
components.responsibility: RolledSize(i), RolledOnDisk(i) and FilesBelow(i) return the column for folders, and Charges() and 0 for files and links. ChildrenLargestFirst(folder) returns ChildRow[] (Entry, OnDisk, Share). It reads ChildCount once, fills each child's on-disk value (rolled for folders, charged for files), and sorts with a struct comparer by OnDisk descending then Entry ascending. That is a total order, so equal sizes come back in listing order on every read even though Array.Sort is unstable. Share = child OnDisk / folder RolledOnDisk, and exactly 0.0 when that total is 0. No order is stored.
components.key_interactions: New partial-class file. ScanStore.cs gains only the `partial` keyword, the Page columns, the Charges change and the append hook, keeping the text that unmerged slice/SL-040 (ef74cd1) also edits small. ChildRow is `readonly record struct ChildRow(int Entry, long OnDisk, double Share)` in the same file.

components.name: Scanner hand-off
components.responsibility: Deletes the Scanner's own copies of the charge rules: the no-bytes branch for links (Scanner.cs:220-222), the folder's own EndOfFile/AllocationSize added to Totals (223-227) and the hardlink branch calling TryAddFileId (235-249). After each append, Totals.Bytes/OnDisk and the TopLevelTracker feed take store.ChargedSize(i)/ChargedOnDisk(i). Totals.Files keeps counting File names only, every name of a hardlinked file included.
components.key_interactions: This must be a deletion, not a copy. If both sides register the ID, the first name finds itself already present, is flagged a duplicate and is charged nowhere. Private TryAddFileId makes that a compile error, and the architecture rule backs it up. After the hand-off, root RolledSize == Totals.Bytes and root FilesBelow == Totals.Files, and each TopLevelRow equals the store's rollup for that child. Those equalities are asserted in the real-tree tests.

components.name: RollupOracle (test helper)
components.responsibility: Two independent checks, both using an explicit stack and never recursion (a 10,000-deep recursion can overflow the test thread's stack and a StackOverflowException kills the host with no message). Expected(model) recomputes every folder's expected size, on-disk size and file count from the test's own input list: its own first-seen HashSet of IDs and its own rule for what charges, with no call into the store's Charges() or flags. CheckStructure(store) walks every folder's subtree over FirstChild/ChildCount and asserts the store's three columns equal the sums, and that each folder's total equals the sum of its children's totals. Failures name the folder index and depth.
components.key_interactions: Expected() is used by synthetic tests, where the input model exists. CheckStructure() is used by real-tree tests, where the expected numbers come from the constructed files. It uses a different algorithm from the store's ancestor walk, and Expected() is also independent of Charges().

components.name: Synthetic rollup, hardlink, leaf and ordering tests
components.responsibility: Cases 1-11: the deep chain, the wide folder, the mixed seeded tree checked after every append on a small one, the three-names hardlink test with FilesBelow asserted at every level, shared ancestors, ID shapes that must not dedupe, link and unreadable leaves with stated sizes, a folder stating its own size, ordering and ties, shares and zero-byte parents. Stores are built only through the public append path, and the test never sets HardlinkDuplicate by hand because it exists to prove the store does.
components.key_interactions: Existing FileId-table tests at ScanStoreTests.cs:77-99 (and any use of TryAddFileId in the budget test) move onto the append path with their assertions preserved. They are migrated, not deleted.

components.name: Ordered-read timing test
components.responsibility: A synthetic store with one 100,000-child folder, seeded sizes and deliberate ties. It makes 10 ChildrenLargestFirst calls, counting the first (cold) one, writes each Stopwatch time and the build configuration to the test output, and asserts every read is under 250 ms.
components.key_interactions: It runs in the Release build the engine already uses (`-c Release`). It carries no Skip and no Trait the default filter excludes, and the architecture rule fences that.

components.name: Real-tree test extensions
components.responsibility: On real temporary NTFS trees, HardlinkTests asserts per-folder RolledOnDisk (one copy on the first name's folder, 0 on the other two), FilesBelow of 1 on each of the three folders, and root FilesBelow == Totals.Files. It includes the stale-listing name that SizeProbe corrects. LinkTests and UnreadableFolderTests assert the leaf adds nothing to its parent's three totals. One new test builds a folder large enough to own a non-zero directory allocation and asserts it is in no total. Every real-tree test runs CheckStructure, asserts root RolledSize == Totals.Bytes, and asserts each TopLevelRow equals the store's rollup for that entry.
components.key_interactions: The build stage runs the whole Core.Tests suite, not the 12-test filter the build-check ran. This slice edits the Scanner, so the project's counting-rule tests (links, hardlinks, on-disk size, long paths, unreadable folders) must all pass on real trees, and none may be skipped.

contracts.name: ScanStore append (existing method, changed behaviour)
contracts.error_cases: InvalidOperationException when the parent is a File, a Link or a folder flagged Unreadable. ArgumentOutOfRangeException when the parent index is not already in the store, which also makes a cycle in the Parent chain impossible. An all-zero ID never deduplicates. A caller-supplied HardlinkDuplicate bit is cleared, never trusted.
contracts.notes: The store applies first-seen dedup and posts each charged file up the Parent chain. Totals are exact between appends: on the writer thread, and after the scan ends or is cancelled. Reading from another thread mid-scan is not part of this contract and belongs to whichever slice first needs it. Callers must keep one writer thread and a deterministic append order, because first-seen charging is repeatable only under that order (spike first-seen-charging-repeatable: no-go with 16 workers).

contracts.name: ScanStore.RolledSize / RolledOnDisk / FilesBelow(int entry)
contracts.error_cases: An out-of-range index behaves like the existing per-entry accessors.
contracts.notes: Folder: sums over every File below at any depth. A hardlink duplicate adds 0 bytes and 1 to FilesBelow. Links and unreadable folders add nothing to any of the three. File: its own charge, and FilesBelow 0. Link: 0, 0, 0. At rest, a folder's three values equal the sums of its children's three values.

contracts.name: ScanStore.ChildrenLargestFirst(int folder) -> ChildRow[]
contracts.error_cases: An empty folder, a file, a link or an Unreadable folder returns an empty array. A folder whose on-disk total is 0 gives every row Share 0.0: never NaN (double 0/0) and never DivideByZeroException (long 0/0).
contracts.notes: Order is OnDisk descending (rolled for folders, charged for files, so a hardlink duplicate ranks as 0), then Entry ascending, which is listing order. It is computed on every call and never stored. It allocates one ChildRow[] per call, about 2.4 MB at 100k children (large object heap). Share is child OnDisk over the folder's RolledOnDisk, and is in [0,1] at rest with no clamp.

contracts.name: ScanStore.ChargedSize / ChargedOnDisk (changed semantics)
contracts.notes: Non-zero only for a File without HardlinkDuplicate. Folders (Unreadable or not) and Links return 0 whatever size they state. SL-040's LargestFiles reads ChargedOnDisk for files only and is unaffected. Expect a textual merge touchpoint in ScanStore.cs with slice/SL-040, kept small on purpose.

contracts.name: Scanner -> ScanTotals and TopLevelTracker
contracts.notes: Totals.Bytes/OnDisk and the TopLevelTracker feed come from the store's charge for each appended entry. Folders' own EndOfFile/AllocationSize leave Totals. The --report schema-1 totals change only where a directory listed a non-zero size of its own. Invariants asserted in real-tree tests: root RolledSize == Totals.Bytes, root RolledOnDisk == Totals.OnDisk, root FilesBelow == Totals.Files, and each TopLevelRow.Bytes/OnDisk/Files equals the store's rollup for that entry. TopLevelTracker is now a second accumulator of numbers the store owns. Retiring it belongs to the slice that draws the tree, not this one.

contracts.name: ScanStore size correction (only if a post-append writer exists)
contracts.notes: If Scanner.cs changes a file's Size or OnDisk after appending it, the change goes through one store method. It computes Charges() before and after and posts the delta up the Parent chain; FilesBelow is unchanged, and a HardlinkDuplicate posts nothing. No other code writes those columns after append. If every probe happens before the append, the method is not added.

key_decisions.decision: Post each charged file up the Parent chain at append time (incremental rollup), not in a post-order pass or a finalise sweep.
key_decisions.rationale: Totals are exact at every cut, including a cancelled scan. There is no DFS-exit or Finalize call the Scanner could forget to make. The walk is an iterative loop, so 10,000 levels are safe. Cost is O(depth) per file, about 60M adds over a 5M-entry scan at realistic depth. It is internal and behind accessors, so the reverse-index sweep (parents precede children) can replace it without touching a contract. The design does not claim exactness for a concurrent reader, because child-before-ancestor posting is visible to one.

key_decisions.decision: Store the three rollup columns per row in the existing Page (about 95 MiB at 5M rows, used on folder rows only), gated by ScanStoreBudgetTests. The pre-decided fallback is a per-row folder-slot column plus per-folder rollups (about 30 MiB).
key_decisions.rationale: It has the same shape as FirstChild/ChildCount, and fixed pages never reallocate. The spike measured 887.8 MiB peak on a throwaway 51 B/row layout that already carried rolled columns, but NOT on the project's ScanStore, whose ID index (an int[] of entry indices) and full-row ID columns differ, so headroom on the real layout is unmeasured. The existing 5M-entry test is the real gate, and the build records its result. A failure switches layout behind the accessors and changes no contract.

key_decisions.decision: The store owns first-seen dedup. Append registers the ID, TryAddFileId becomes private to the store, the Scanner's copies of the charge rules are deleted, and existing tests that fed the ID table by hand migrate onto append.
key_decisions.rationale: Criterion 2's test is store-level and must prove the store applies the rule. Two registrations flag the first name as its own duplicate and charge the file nowhere. Private visibility makes that a compile error, and the architecture rule covers the case where the builder must keep it internal.

key_decisions.decision: Single writer plus deterministic append order is a documented invariant of the store. This slice keeps the Scanner single-threaded and does not try to make first-seen charging parallel-safe.
key_decisions.rationale: The spike measured first-seen charging with 16 workers as a no-go: 68 folders swung by more than 10 MiB across 5 runs (WinSxS by 587 MiB) while the control moved 0 B and the root total was conserved. A future parallel scanner must serialize appends deterministically or change criterion 2's rule (ncdu-style per-subtree counting is the known alternative). Either changes a contract every totals reader depends on. The invariant is written into the append doc so the next person finds it.

key_decisions.decision: Only a File that is not a HardlinkDuplicate charges bytes. Folders (readable, or Unreadable with a stated size) and Links charge 0 and count as 0 files. Append under a File, Link or Unreadable folder, or under a parent not yet in the store, throws.
key_decisions.rationale: Criterion 4 holds by rule instead of by every caller remembering it, and the survey's Charges() gap (Unreadable keeps its stated size) is closed. 'Parent's totals unchanged' is read as all three totals, so a link is not counted as a file. Validating the parent index also rules out a cycle in the ancestor walk.

key_decisions.decision: Scan-wide Totals and the TopLevelTracker feed take the store's per-entry charge, so folders' own EndOfFile/AllocationSize leave Totals and root RolledSize/RolledOnDisk/FilesBelow equal Totals.Bytes/OnDisk/Files by construction.
key_decisions.rationale: Criteria 1 and 4 define folder totals as sums over files below, and Scanner.cs:223-227 was adding folders' own sizes. Two counting rules would give the header total and the tree's root total different numbers. The equalities become assertions in the real-tree tests. It changes user-visible totals and --report only where a directory listed a non-zero size, and the full suite plus the big-folder test show where. This is raised as an open question because it changes numbers a person reads.

key_decisions.decision: Sort children on every read (OnDisk descending, then Entry ascending) and store no per-folder order. Share is 0.0 when the folder's on-disk total is 0, with no clamp.
key_decisions.rationale: This departs from the architecture line that the store holds children sorted largest first, and the timing test is what measures it against the 250 ms budget. The estimate is tens of milliseconds for 100k structs. It costs no memory against a tight budget and is never stale while sizes change. If the test fails, a cached order can sit behind the same call. The Entry tiebreak makes the order total, so 'stable' holds even though Array.Sort is unstable. Share is on-disk based because the order is; U-019's online-only files reach the zero case for real.

key_decisions.decision: The brute-force oracle is independent of the store's charge rule. Synthetic tests recompute expected totals from the test's own input model (own first-seen HashSet, own rule for what charges) and never call Charges() or read HardlinkDuplicate. Real-tree tests use a structural check plus expected numbers from the constructed files. No recursion anywhere.
key_decisions.rationale: An oracle that sums ChargedSize shares the very rule under test, so a Charges() defect (the Unreadable one the survey found) would pass. Recursion at 10,000 depth kills the test host silently.

key_decisions.decision: The timing test asserts every one of the 10 reads, including the cold first, is under 250 ms, and logs the build configuration. It has no JIT-optimised guard.
key_decisions.rationale: The user's first expand of a folder is cold, and the maximum is stricter than the mean. A pass in Debug implies a pass in Release, so a guard adds nothing and could only fail a Debug run for a false reason. The engine already runs `-c Release`. The 6x or greater margin over the estimate absorbs the load of two slices building at once.

key_decisions.decision: New read code lives in a partial ScanStore.Rollup.cs. Edits to ScanStore.cs are limited to the `partial` keyword, the Page columns, the Charges rule and the append hook.
key_decisions.rationale: Unmerged slice/SL-040 also edits ScanStore.cs (Size/OnDisk made internal, LargestFiles). Commit-slice resolves no conflicts, so a small, local edit surface is the protection. Whichever slice merges second rebases and re-runs the store tests.

architecture_rules.name: the Scanner does not register file IDs or set the duplicate flag; the store does
architecture_rules.because: The store applies first-seen dedup inside append. If the Scanner registers the ID too, the first name finds its own ID already present, is flagged a duplicate and its bytes are charged nowhere. Every folder total under it is silently low, and the whole suite can stay green if only synthetic tests run.

architecture_rules.name: the store does not know about the Scanner
architecture_rules.because: The counting rule lives in the store so criteria 1-6 can be proved on synthetic entry streams with no disk. A store that reaches back into the Scanner makes those tests need a real drive and lets a second copy of the rule grow in the Scanner.

architecture_rules.name: the rollup and timing tests are never skipped or filtered out
architecture_rules.because: The project's testing constraint says counting-rule tests are never skipped, and criterion 6 is a measured number. A skipped or default-filtered test reports green while proving nothing, which is the failure this slice's cases exist to prevent.

cases.shape: a chain 10,000 folders deep with one file at every level
cases.why: The append walk must be a loop and the oracle iterative. A recursive walk overflows the stack at this depth and a StackOverflowException kills the test host with no message. Every ancestor must gain every file below it.

cases.shape: one folder with 100,000 direct children, 1,000 of them subfolders holding files
cases.why: Very wide fan-out crosses several 64Ki-entry page boundaries, and every child posts to the same parent. It is also the store shape the timing case reuses.

cases.shape: empty folders, nested empty folders, an empty root, and a seeded ~50k-entry mixed tree (reused IDs, links, unreadable folders with stated sizes, 0-byte files), with the oracle run after every append on a small one
cases.why: A folder with no children never posts and must read 0/0/0. Checking after each append proves totals stay exact at every cut, which is what a cancelled scan leaves behind.

cases.behaviour: count a hardlinked file once (C2, C3)
cases.shape: one ID under three names in three different folders, appended in a fixed order
cases.why: Root equals one copy and only the first name's folder chain is charged. Later names carry the flag the store set itself and add 0 bytes but 1 file at every level. The order is fixed because first-seen charging depends on it.

cases.behaviour: count a hardlinked file once (C2, C3)
cases.shape: names that share an ancestor or a parent (a/x and a/b/y; two names inside one folder)
cases.why: A shared ancestor must gain the bytes once but the count twice. A walk that posts per name without checking the flag would double-charge exactly there.

cases.shape: IDs that must not match: two files with an all-zero ID, and two files with the same low 64 bits but different high 64 bits
cases.why: Zero means 'no ID' (SMB or FAT) and deduplicating it drops real bytes silently. The 128-bit compare must use both halves. The existing Scanner behaviour for a zero ID is carried over and asserted.

cases.behaviour: keep links and unopened folders as leaves (C4)
cases.shape: a link (Size 5000, OnDisk 8192) and an Unreadable folder (4096/4096) beside one normal file, plus a later append naming a File, the Link or the Unreadable folder as parent
cases.why: Charges() before this slice let the Unreadable folder keep its stated size. The parent's three totals (size, on-disk, files) must equal the normal file alone, both leaves must have ChildCount 0 and charge 0, and the bad append must throw.

cases.behaviour: keep a folder's own size out of every total (C1, C4)
cases.shape: a readable folder that states its own non-zero size (synthetic 4096/4096, and a real NTFS folder large enough to own a directory allocation)
cases.why: The Scanner used to add a folder's own EndOfFile/AllocationSize to Totals. Folder totals are file sums, so root RolledSize == Totals.Bytes only holds once that branch is gone.

cases.shape: a folder of mixed files and subfolders with equal on-disk sizes and one hardlink duplicate (0 B), read three times
cases.why: A folder ranks by its rolled on-disk total, not its own stated size. Array.Sort is unstable, so listing order for ties comes only from the Entry tiebreak. Every read must return the same order, with the duplicate last.

cases.behaviour: give each child its share of the parent (C5)
cases.shape: children whose shares are 3/4 and 1/4 (exact), 1/3 (within 1e-12), on a finished folder whose shares sum to 1
cases.why: Share divides by the folder's on-disk total, not its logical size. The sum-to-one check ties the ordered read to the rollup invariant, so a rollup error shows up as a share error.

cases.behaviour: give each child its share of the parent (C5)
cases.shape: a parent whose on-disk total is 0: an empty folder, a folder of only hardlink duplicates, and one holding online-only files (logical size above 0, on-disk 0). Also a File, a Link and an Unreadable folder passed as the folder
cases.why: In double, 0/0 is NaN without any error, and in long it throws. The criterion allows neither. U-019 shows online-only OneDrive folders reach this case in real use. A non-folder argument must return an empty array, not throw.

cases.shape: one folder with 100,000 children and many ties, 10 reads with the cold first counted, Release build
cases.why: Criterion 6 is a number. The cold read includes JIT, and each call allocates a large-object-heap array. The machine may be busy with another slice's build, so every read is asserted, not only the mean.

cases.behaviour: count bytes through the real Scanner on NTFS (C1-C4)
cases.shape: the existing real temporary trees (three-name hardlink with a stale-listing name, link, unreadable folder, on-disk size, long path) extended with per-folder rollup assertions, root == Totals, and TopLevelRow == rollup
cases.why: Only the Scanner path shows a post-append size write bypassing the posting, double registration of an ID (a file charged nowhere), Totals.Files disagreeing with FilesBelow, or a second accumulator (TopLevelTracker) drifting. The full Core.Tests suite runs, not the 12-test subset.

cases.behaviour: hold a full scan in memory (C1)
cases.shape: 5,000,000 entries carrying the three rollup columns, with one 100,000-child folder
cases.why: The spike verdict is conditional (887.8 MiB on a throwaway layout) and did not measure the project's ScanStore with these columns. ScanStoreBudgetTests is the gate. Its result is recorded, and a failure triggers the folder-slot fallback.

proposals.note: The only proposal. Taken as the core, with these changes: independent oracle, TryAddFileId private, parent-index validation, TopLevelTracker pinned to the rollups, no share clamp, no JIT guard, and no claim of exactness for concurrent readers. Two prior-art entries were downgraded from cited to recalled.

payload.coherence_check:
One proposal, so there is no composition across proposals to check. Nothing here has yet survived a disagreement, and that is the first thing to argue with. The claims most worth attacking are: (a) sort-on-read needs only tens of milliseconds at 100k children, which is an estimate and not a measurement, and the timing test is what settles it; (b) the per-row columns fit the memory budget on the project's real ScanStore, which is also unmeasured, because the spike used a throwaway layout; (c) folders' own allocation should leave scan-wide Totals.

Checks I ran on the proposal's own invariants:
1. It said totals are 'exact at any point' and also that readers are lock-free. Those conflict, because posting is child-then-ancestor, so a concurrent reader can see a child larger than its parent. That is why the proposal needed a clamp. I kept the strong claim only for between-appends and for after a stop or cancel, dropped the clamp, and left concurrent readers to the first slice that needs them.
2. The store owns dedup, the Scanner feeds Totals from store charges, and a Scanner-side ID registration would charge a file nowhere. I made TryAddFileId private, added the architecture rule, and named the existing FileId-table tests (ScanStoreTests.cs:77-99, possibly the budget test) as migrations onto the append path.
3. The proposal's oracle summed the store's ChargedSize, so it shared the rule under test. I split it into a model-based Expected() and a structural CheckStructure().
4. TopLevelTracker holds a second copy of root-child totals, and the proposal left it untouched. If it kept its own charge decisions, the tree and the header would disagree. It is now fed from the store and asserted equal in the real-tree tests.
5. Unreadable parent throws versus late flagging: the Scanner opens a folder after its row exists and flags it before any child is appended, so the guard never fires on the real path. A late flag never un-posts anything.

What the earlier stages did not record, which I needed and did not raise as an obligation because each is a one-grep fact with both branches designed: the build-check should have recorded (i) whether Scanner.cs writes a file's Size or OnDisk after the append (SizeProbe), which decides if the correction method exists; (ii) the budget test's threshold and its current measured peak; (iii) whether Totals.Files counts links; (iv) whether any existing test's expected value includes a folder's own allocation; and (v) how ScanStoreTests.cs and the budget test call TryAddFileId. The build's first step greps for them. The spike measured a throwaway store, so the memory verdict is conditional and not a yes for this layout. Its single-writer constraint is honoured and its key-only ID-set constraint holds by construction.

Merge seam: slice/SL-040 (ef74cd1, unmerged) edits ScanStore.cs. The rollup reads sit in a separate partial file and ScanStore.cs edits are kept minimal. LargestFiles reads ChargedOnDisk for files only, so the Charges() change does not alter it, but whichever slice merges second must re-run the store tests.

Any rules this design declares go through the engine's append onto the existing rules file (Q-010). This slice does not create that file.

Nothing was contested by anybody, so no disagreement is classified as decidable. The memory layout and the correction-method branch are settled by the build and change no contract.
taste_disagreements: Sort-on-read with no stored order departs from the architecture line that the store holds children sorted largest first. A reviewer may prefer a cached or stored order.
Rollup columns sit on every row (simple, 95 MiB) rather than a folder-slot layout (about 30 MiB, an extra indirection). A reviewer may prefer the smaller one up front.
I dropped the proposal's share clamp and its JIT-optimised guard on the timing test. The proposal kept both as defensive measures.
New store reads live in a partial-class file ScanStore.Rollup.cs, a boundary chosen to shrink the SL-040 merge surface. A reviewer may prefer them inline or in a separate type.
The oracle is split into Expected(model) and CheckStructure(store). A reviewer may want a single helper.
open_questions: Should scan-wide Totals and --report stop counting a folder's own allocation (a big directory's index)? This design says yes, per criteria 1 and 4. It changes reported totals only where a directory lists a non-zero size. If the person wants that space shown, it needs its own column, not RolledOnDisk.

Criterion 2's 'first name seen charges the bytes' is repeatable only with one writer thread and a fixed append order (spike: no-go with 16 workers). U-012 says per-file queries are 5x slower than listing, so a parallel scanner is likely later. Should that future slice serialize appends deterministically, or should criterion 2 be re-agreed as per-subtree counting, which lets children sum to more than their parent?
whats_reused: The flat, index-addressed Page columns (64Ki-entry pages), Parent, and the contiguous FirstChild/ChildCount child blocks in src/FsAnalyser.Core/Store/ScanStore.cs
The existing first-seen FileId index (open-addressing int[] of entry indices, key-only, reads the ID columns) and Charges() as the single charge rule, both now called from append
The Scanner's single-threaded DFS and its Totals, kept, but fed from the store

prior_art.pattern: A flat, index-addressed arena where each node names its parent and children by index and sizes and file counts are aggregated bottom-up during the walk, so a node's size is already its subtree total. This is the shape of ScanStore plus the rollup columns.
Count a hard-linked file once, under the first path that reaches it. This is the same first-seen rule as criterion 2.

Inode dedup across parallel walkers uses a seen-set sharded over 64 mutex-protected HashSets, with real post-order directory completion. This is the machinery parallelism needs and a single writer does not, which is why this design chose incremental posting.

A result where a hardlink was counted as zero because another link was seen first is flagged scan-order dependent and kept out of the on-disk cache. This confirms the spike's no-go on first-seen charging across arrival orders. The proposal marked it cited, but the URL is not in the fetched block I was given, so I record it as recalled.

Each directory carries its own size and count and keeps a read error on the directory, so an unreadable directory stays in the tree, and files of unknown size count as files but add no bytes. The proposal marked it cited, but the URL is not in the fetched block I was given, so I record it as recalled.
GNU du counts a multiply-linked file once, at its first encounter in traversal order, so per-directory numbers depend on traversal order.

ncdu counts a hardlinked inode once within each directory subtree that contains any of its names. That is order-independent, but children can sum to more than their parent. It is the known escape if the scanner ever goes parallel, and it would replace criterion 2.
